Noah Smith 🐇🇺🇸🇺🇦🇹🇼 (@Noahpinion)

I will never cease to be amazed at conservatives' ability to invent a Fantasy Obama in their heads to get angry at

Japan might suffer the same outsourcing of state capacity that America suffered


愚泥 (@DOVGQ)

東大卒が官僚ではなくコンサルに行きたがるのは、官僚がブラックであるだけでなく、官自体がやるべきことをコンサルに丸投げしているから、官から受注しているコンサルに行った方が国策の現場に携われるというのがあると聞いたことがあり、問題の根は深いと思った。



— https://nitter.net/DOVGQ/status/2051804303124508918#m

Why do people assume that ancient architectural styles would carry through to the modern day? Do modern skyscrapers look like old European church steeples or castle towers? No.


Alex Patrascu (@maxescu)

A vision of a modern Tenochtitlan in 2026, in a timeline where the Aztec Empire repelled Spanish conquest and modernized on its own terms.

Enjoy:

Video
  





— https://nitter.net/maxescu/status/2051700990366060763#m

For my entire childhood I wanted this squirrel as a pet.

Then A) I got to play with an actual pet squirrel, and B) some crazy Nazi lady used this squirrel as an avatar.

Well, so much for that dream.

Russia really has two options left: 1) accept a war outcome that everyone will recognize as a loss, or 2) use strategic nuclear weapons on Ukrainian cities.

These bloggers are advocating for (2), but they are too scared to say it explicitly.


Jay in Kyiv (@JayinKyiv)

Increasingly now reliant on the fictitious narrative that Russia isn't winning only because they've been constrained by a moral code that prevents them from waging REAL WAR, another of Russia's most popular military bloggers says
It’s weird, watching the Daredevil show and seeing Kingpin murder people with his bare hands and set heavily-armed maniacs against civilians, and knowing he’s still a better human being than Trump. ￼

Hey, Universe!

STOP KILLING THE WRONG OLD MEN! 

www.huffpost.com/entry/ted-tu...

Leslie Bibb is awesome and I would never want to body shame anybody, or question the choices they make for their own bodies, especially knowing the pressure that actresses feel to stay thin. But this is more carbohydrates than this woman has eaten since the Obama administration.
If I were a celebrity I would live in constant fear that I might get invited to the Met Gala.
Luke Skywalker is the ultimate Generation X icon because, like so many of us, he learned everything he needed to know from a Muppet.
RFK 100% thinks he saved somebody from being attacked by this starling.

Yeah, I think you nailed it. I mean, who else would we consider? John Goodman, Dan Lauria, Ray Romano, Tony Danza, Reginald VelJohnson, and the Modern Family dads seem like the only viable options and Gross tops any of them.

Who else would even be in the conversation? Neil Flynn? Bill Kirchenbauer?
Nuts! I only lived in NYC for one year under Giuliani. I’m gonna be so far back in line I’m gonna have to take bathroom breaks during my wait!
Upon reflection I would swap Friends and Star Trek: TNG for Head of the Class and maybe West Wing.

Name your top 15 TV shows ever, gut instincts only—

Simpsons
SNL
Sesame Street
Cheers
The Daily Show with John Stewart
The Office
Quantum Leap
The Cosby Show
Jeopardy!
The West Wing 
Parks and Recreation
30 Rock
Mr. Rogers’ Neighborhood 
You Can’t Do That on Television
Head of the Class

Hope this doesn’t sound like I’m trying to brag but I remember having the opposite experience once when my kids were Happy Meal age. I said “Hot Wheels” and the cashier INSISTED that I say “boy.” It was weird. (I think English might not have been her first language so maybe I’m the asshole.)

Mary Poppins: You know, you *can* say it backwards, which is "docious-ali-expi-istic-fragil-cali-rupus" 

Me: Well … that’s not exactly backwards. You sort of broke the word up into two-syllable segments and said them in reverse order except for “super” which you SORT OF pronounced backwards?

If you didn’t know anything about Disney princesses or the stories they’re based on, and you saw pictures, a list of their names, and brief descriptions  of them, you’d assume the one with ice powers was Snow White and the one in the quasi-German outfit was Elsa.
What? Am I running an AirBaMBi here?

Mary Poppins: That's a piecrust promise. Easily made, easily broken.

Me: Okay, first off, if you think making a pie crust from scratch is easy, you and I are coming at this from VERY different perspectives.
[Obligatory “End of the World as We Know It” joke.]
I assume the creatures that ate ginkgo were an ancient species of stench beetles?
The apostrophe placement bothers me, though I do kind of like the idea that there is one person named “Little Picasso” and they opened up a daycare.
In my defense, he was advertising Jell-O products long before the pudding pops came on the market!
Could development economics be more useful?
AI's big messaging pivot. Some top AI leaders now say their technology will create jobs. Should we believe them?
California's "billionaire tax" is the wrong approach. Left-populist instincts are leading to silly policy ideas.
Roundup #81: Back to our regular programming. National debt; AI cyberattacks; Phone bans; AI and coding jobs; Millennials vs. Boomers; Public order; California YIMBYism
Scoring the Jensen-Dwarkesh debate. Export controls are holding back Chinese AI. Should we keep them?
The moderately easy problem of consciousness. Before deciding if computers are self-aware, let's figure out how humans become self-aware.
Why shoplifting is bad. It may feel like a small act of rebellion, but it hurts a lot of people who don't deserve it.
Is China's soft power really rising, or is America's just crumbling?
No, America is not in a "stealth manufacturing boom"
Updated thoughts on industrial policy. Economic consensus is changing, but it has a long way to go.
Hasan Piker is bad for the Democrats. Republicans embraced extremist ideology and it backfired on them. Democrats shouldn't follow suit.
You are what you consume. Personal identity should come from the things we get to choose for ourselves.
What if a few AI companies end up with all the money and power?. Contemplating the grim future of the "Robot Lords".
Will Americans want more housing if it looks prettier?
Yes, assimilation is good. Building a unified American culture isn't about bullying people; it's about living together in peace.
